records.summary: The model is understandable only if execution evidence, protected-data boundaries and executor-independent work are made explicit; adjacent tooling is secondary.

items.label: Execution history
items.reason: The central production argument depends on being able to reconstruct consequential work after it happened.

items.label: Protected data separation
items.reason: The control layer is incomplete if observing orchestration implicitly grants broad access to protected business data.

items.label: Human-agent task equivalence
items.reason: Executor-independent tasks make escalation and handoff understandable without turning human review into an unrelated exception process.

records.summary: Temporal becomes coherent only when Workflow Execution, Event History and Activity retry semantics are understood as separate responsibilities.

items.label: Workflow Execution
items.reason: The reader needs a stable unit of long-running orchestration before Worker failure and recovery can make sense.

items.label: Event History
items.reason: Durable recovery depends on understanding where workflow progress is represented independently of one Worker process.

items.label: Activity execution
items.reason: Side-effecting work must be separated from deterministic orchestration to understand retry behavior and failure boundaries.

items.label: Idempotency under retry
items.reason: The practical boundary of durable execution is missed if repeated external effects are assumed to become exactly-once automatically.

records.summary: OPA needs two prerequisites: policy as explicit decision logic and a clear boundary between deciding permission and enforcing the protected action.

items.label: Policy as code
items.reason: OPA only makes sense once policy is treated as explicit, reviewable decision logic rather than hidden application branching.

items.label: Policy decision / enforcement separation
items.reason: The architecture is misread if the policy engine is treated as the component that performs the protected business action.

items.label: Policy distribution
items.reason: Operational use becomes clearer when policy and data lifecycle are separated from application deployment through bundles or equivalent mechanisms.

records.summary: ReAct requires a compact loop model first; production governance is useful boundary context but is not a prerequisite for understanding the paper mechanism itself.

items.label: ReAct loop
items.reason: The paper's mechanism is the repeated relationship between reasoning, environment action and returned observation.

items.label: Reasoning trace
items.reason: A reasoning step must be distinguished from an external action because only the latter changes or queries the environment.

items.label: Observation grounding
items.reason: The value of acting is not only execution; returned evidence changes what the model can reason about next.

items.label: Controlled execution
items.reason: This prior model is useful for separating ReAct's cognitive loop from authorization, durability and outcome verification in production.

records.summary: The source needs only the retrieval event and the immediate-versus-delayed distinction; broader learning-science machinery would add noise at this stage.

items.label: Retrieval practice
items.reason: The testing effect cannot be understood unless retrieval is treated as a learning event rather than only an assessment event.

items.label: Immediate performance / delayed retention gap
items.reason: The study's central result depends on ranking learning conditions differently immediately and after a meaningful delay.

items.label: Metacognitive confidence gap
items.reason: Confidence matters as a secondary concept because feeling fluent immediately can diverge from what is retrievable later.
